name: Timote-Cuica
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Urban (2018) A New Approach to the Reconstitution of the Pronunciation of Timote-Cuica; Rivet (1927) La famille linguistique Timote - neither reachable online; language extinct, attested mainly in wordlists

sources.citation: Urban, Matthias. 2018. A New Approach to the Reconstitution of the Pronunciation of Timote-Cuica (Venezuelan Andes). Cadernos de Etnolingüística 6(1): 31-50.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Whole article read (vowels sect. 4, consonants sect. 5, conclusion sect. 6): reconstitutes [ɨ], nasal vowels, prenasalized stops, two fricative places, a glottal; contains no discussion of stress or accent at all (the word 'unstressed' occurs once, p. 47, about the Spanish loan aguardiente).

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2009 [updated]. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos: entry MUTÚS / TIMOTE.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic entry; says Arrieta 1998 offers a phonological typology and Rivet 1927 a comparative study; nothing on stress. Supplied the venue of Urban 2018.

sources.citation: Arrieta E., Anita. 1998. Tipología fonológica del timote. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 24(1): 85-100. DOI 10.15517/rfl.v24i1.20431
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Runs through Constenla's typological rubros 43-81 (vowel/consonant contrasts, tone) and gives a phoneme inventory (pp. 98-99); no rubro on stress and no statement on accent. Only prosodic remark is Rubro 49, p. 90: 'Los datos, tal como han sido transcritos, no permiten determinar oposiciones tonales.' Cited forms carry the sources' acute accents (kushís, tigús, surí, kismí) without comment.

sources.citation: Arrieta E., Anita. 1993. Tipología morfosintáctica del Timote. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la Universidad de Costa Rica 19(2): 99-110. DOI 10.15517/rfl.v19i2.20221
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Morphosyntax only; nothing on stress (a full-text search for stress/accent acent/tónic/prosod: no hits).

sources.citation: Jahn, Alfredo. 1927. Los aborígenes del occidente de Venezuela: su historia, etnografía y afinidades lingüísticas. Caracas: Lit. y Tip. del Comercio.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Timote chapter (pp. 325-327) explains that the orthography is Urrecheaga's ('La ortografía empleada es la original Urrecheaga', p. 326); the appendix 'Vocabulario de la lengua Timote' (pp. 396ff.) marks acute accents on many words (ki-kushám, ki-kóngk, ki-kubú, ki-kuspéch, ki-kumeú) but gives no rule; no occurrence of 'acento'/'sílaba' in a linguistic sense.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1927. La famille linguistique Timote (Venezuela). International Journal of American Linguistics 4(2-4): 137-167. DOI 10.1086/463765
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: History of the tribes and of the wordlists (Lares, Febres Cordero, Fonseca, Urrecheaga) plus a comparative Timote-Kuika vocabulary; reproduces the collectors' acute accents (kué, hussá, chirúp) but says nothing about accent or pronunciation (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/prononc/orthograph: no hits; Urban 2018:35 also notes Rivet 'bypassed' phonetic comments).

sources.citation: Febres Cordero, Tulio. 1921. Historia de los Andes: procedencia y lengua de los aborígenes. Mérida: Tip. 'El Lápiz'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. VII 'Ortología andina' (pp. 91-101) is the only first-hand pronunciation description: two non-Spanish vowels (ou, i/u), remarks on b, c, ch, d, g, j, l, a nasal 'ronquido' onset, r, tz; nothing on accent or stress. His wordlist marks accents (cassúm, capsín, chirúp, tabís) without comment.

sources.citation: Ernst, A. 1885. Ueber die Reste der Ureinwohner in den Gebirgen von Mérida. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 17: 190-197.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Reprints Lares's wordlists (Mirripú, Mocochies, Migurí, Timotes, El Morro); sole pronunciation note, p. 193 fn. 2: 'Die Aussprache ist nach den Regeln der spanischen Sprache zu verstehen' (pronunciation to be read by Spanish rules, i.e. accents as in Spanish orthography); no rule of stress placement.

sources.citation: Fonseca, Amílcar. 2005 [1955]. Orígenes trujillanos, vol. 1, ch. 'Dialectología', pp. 261-338. Trujillo: Fondo Editorial Arturo Cardozo.

sources.note: Most extensive Cuica data with observer commentary (Fonseca states e.g. that <kuu> is disyllabic, per Urban 2018:48); the likeliest place for a first-hand remark on accent.
